children: Andy Burnham will drive home his pledge to bring more essential services back into public control, telling MPs in the Commons on Tuesday that it will be the only way to improve growth across the country. Burnham will address the house for the first time in 16 years from the frontbench, and six weeks since he became prime minister, after spending the summer recess announcing a slew of policies that will now be put before MPs. – Guardian

Germany’s economy has shown surprising signs of strength lately. Consumer, investor and business confidence has rebounded, factories are taking more orders and growth is the fastest since 2022. This wasn’t on most economists’ bingo cards for 2026. Beleaguered by high energy costs, cut-throat Chinese competition and swathes of red tape, Germany is perennially called “the sick man of Europe”. – Telegraph

ChatGPT risks being forced to pay hefty fines under strict new rules enforced by Brussels. The AI chatbot has four months to meet EU content moderation rules after it was placed under its toughest regulatory regime for online services. The EU has designated ChatGPT a so-called “Very Large Online Search Engine” under the Digital Services Act (DSA), meaning that it has until the end of January to comply with additional reporting obligations. It is the first chatbot to be classified as a search engine by the EU. – Telegraph

The crisis in Capita’s civil service pension contract has intensified after the waiting list for retirement quotes and bereavement payouts more than doubled to 30,061 at the start of August. The London-listed outsourcer has seen its backlog of outstanding pension estimates almost double from 9,468 to 17,014 over the three weeks to August 7, while the waiting list for survivor benefits almost tripled from 4,750 to 13,047, as the group battles to get to grips with the scheme. – The Times
